utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber received this morning another bundle of material which has been given to the parties. I do understand that there's a cover page which briefly sets out what is contained in this material. The parties can consider whether it's of any use to bring it to the attention of the Chamber. The Chamber will not look at it, apart from having a look at the summary provided in this cover page once it has been translated. Then, Mr. Krajisnik, I was informed that you would like to add something to one of the things you said, so part of your testimony last Friday. I'll give you an opportunity to do so, but not until after I have reminded you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the very beginning of your testimony. So therefore, if you'd like to add something, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I only wish to correct something, introduce a small correction into my statement. I said that together with Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Koljevic, the late Mr. Koljevic, I went to Herzegovina after the session of the 12th of May. I have checked this, and I did go before the session to Nevesinje, that is. That's one correction. And the second correction, I mentioned Vance's book, but that was an error. The book, The Balkan Odyssey was written by David Owen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik, for these corrections. Then Mr. Tieger or Mr. Harmon, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik on Friday you were testifying about the strategic objectives, and in your evidence found at lines -- page -- 17:22:32, you said that not a single deputy, not even Mr. Beli understood Mr. Karadzic to be saying that the strategic objectives were strategic priorities to be achieved by military means, you said: "Not even Mr. Beli nor any other deputy." Later on in your examination Mr. Tieger, at 17:03:30, suggested to you that you and other members of the Bosnian Serb leadership knew full well and intended that the effort to achieve those goals would be pursued through negotiations and through military efforts. And your answer at 17:03:54 was: "It was not so." Mr. Krajisnik, at the 16th Session, General Mladic was present when those goals were enunciated. In addition, there were other military figures who were present at the 16th Session. Can you identify those other military figures besides General Mladic who were present when the strategic objectives were announced by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, but apart from Mr. Mladic there were other military representatives there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Then if you can't recall we'll -- we won't pursue that further. What I'd like to do, have you examine --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If Mr. Krajisnik can be given the bundle starting with Exhibit 214. We'll distribute those now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, just for your information I'm going to be directing you to tab 218. Mr. Krajisnik, at tab 218 is a document that has been previously exhibited. It is P64, P529, Hanson tab 255. It is the analysis of the combat readiness and activities of the Army of the Republika Srpska in 1992. It is from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska. It is a strictly confidential military secret. And this document, Mr. Krajisnik, was, as you recall, the result of a meeting that took place. If you turn to -- in the B/C/S, Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If Your Honours turn to pages 4 and -- I'm sorry, the second and third pages in the text following the cover -- following the cover sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let me see where I can locate that for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If my learned friend has a spare bundle and can have it given to Mr. Sladojevic and he'll assist as best he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 1st Drina Corps appears on page 135 in the B/C/S version, and that's what I find on page -- on the -- as you said, Mr. -- oh, no, that's the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have it, Your Honour, now in a different bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, it is found with the ERN pages the last four digits are 7343, if you look at upper right-hand corner, and it follows the cover sheet. It's pages 5, 6, and 7. Mr. Krajisnik, it looks like this. You must have the same copy that I have, so let me pass this to you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, the last four digits in B/C/S ERN number always start with 74 in my copy not 73.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik's copy does not have apparently the pages that I'm referring to, my copy does not have those pages. So Mr. Krajisnik has been given a copy with the relevant pages. Now, does Your Honour -- do Your Honours have copies of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you referred to the pages as the third and the fourth after the cover page, so we have that, but whether these are the same as you have in mind is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, it's the plan, Your Honour, and it starts on the upper right-hand corner. The ERN number is 01103022. It should be the first page after the cover sheet of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have pages -- I have a numbering through at the bottom starting with 154, 155, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Apparently there's been a mistake, Your Honour. Your Honours don't have it. I can move on. It's not that important. It's in the exhibit itself, Your Honour, and what the exhibit shows and what Mr. Krajisnik has in front of him is essentially the plan that was the agenda for the meeting that gave rise to ultimately this report. It's in the exhibit itself. I don't intend to question at length about this. I'll move on from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let's move on to the contents of this particular report. What I'd like to do is to refer you, Mr. Krajisnik, to page --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Court, first of all, to page 158 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Krajisnik, for -- in the B/C/S it is -- the ERN number has the last four digits of 7476.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. And this -- first of all, it's the part of the report that deals with the basic characteristics of the operational and tactical utilisation of the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Your Honours turn to page 159, the first full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krajisnik, this should be found for your benefit on the next page. It is page that has the ERN numbers, last four digits 7477. And I'm referring, Mr. Krajisnik, to the top paragraph. In this then, Mr. Krajisnik, this report on the army on the basic characteristics of the operational and tactical utilisation of the Army of the Republika Srpska, I'm going read to you from the passage I've directed your attention to: "The strategic objectives of our war which were promptly defined and set before the Main Staff of the Army of RS, the commands and units, served as general guidelines upon which we planned the actual operations and concerted battles. This means that objectives were set before us rather than specific tasks spelled out, although the president of the republic, that is the supreme commander of the armed forces of RS, did orally assign a number of tasks which were of general and vital significance to our struggle in protecting the Serbian people and its territories. The Main Staff of the Army of RS translated the set objectives and tasks into general and individual missions of the Army of RS and of the individual operational and tactical formations with the goals of every individual combat action, operation, or battle being specifically defined." Mr. Krajisnik, if you read further down the page you'll see a number of bullet points, and I'm going to direct your attention to some of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the same page, 159, the last sentence in that paragraph from which I read it says: "We can -- we can say with certainty that even though often without an operational tactical link, i.e., contact, our operations of the operations of all units are mutually supportive in pursuit of single goals which we have defined such as ..." And the first bullet point is: "The defence of the Serbian people against genocide at the hands of Muslim/Croat forces." And the second -- the third bullet point is: "The liberation of territories which are ours and which belong to us by historical birth right."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krajisnik, what did that last bullet point mean? "The liberation of territories which are ours and which belong to us by historic birth right," what did that mean?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is military terminology. I can only speculate and say that they had to liberate Serb ethnic areas that had been taken by the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, this language echoes very clearly language -- political language that we have heard in the Assembly sessions and we have seen in other documents. So, Mr. Krajisnik, this should not be a turn of a phrase that is a surprise to you. What specifically do you believe "the liberation of territories which are ours and which belong to us by historical birth right," what do you think that means? What do you think the army understood that as they say a goal that they pursued?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot interpret what the army did, but all this here is not linked to the strategic objectives adopted at the Assembly of the 12th of May. This is a plan of the army. The army was established and was operating in 1992, and it was carrying out its activities. I can only guess if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in your guessing, Mr. Krajisnik. You said at the -- in your evidence on Friday that the military strategic objectives were not interpreted -- essentially these were objectives to be pursued by the army. And we see in this report, Mr. Krajisnik, according to this report the strategic objectives were promptly defined before the Main Staff, promptly defined before the commands, promptly defined before the units, and they served as general guidelines for actual operations and battles. So there -- I'm submitting to you, Mr. Krajisnik, there was a link between what Dr. Karadzic said and the actions and activities of the army. Is that something that you do not agree with?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree at all. Military strategic goals differ from political strategic objectives. Karadzic, as the supreme commander, may have discussed military strategic objectives with them but at the Assembly their strategic objectives were exclusively political ones, intended for negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And are you saying that they were not intended to convey a message or a programme of goals to the military?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Today I handed over documents which go to deny this and which show that both Mladic and Mrs. Plavsic and the minister of the MUP said that every cease-fire had to be respected. This means that he understood the messages sent by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krajisnik, let's first of all take a look at your answer. I want to make sure that I understand it. Are you saying that when Dr. Karadzic enunciated the strategic objectives at the 16th Assembly Session in the presence of General Mladic and in the presence of other military officers, those goals were in no way intended to form part of the military planning that was to implement the programme of war that was being pursued at the time by the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Mr. Karadzic enunciated the platform for negotiations, what we were to advocate at negotiations. And he also advocated the continuation of the conference. This has absolutely nothing to do with military objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look, Mr. Krajisnik, if we could, at tab 195.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If that bundle could be distributed as well. This 195, Your Honour, has been previously exhibited. It's Prosecution Exhibit 244.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the exhibit that is in tab 195, Prosecution Exhibit 244, is a document that we have seen before in this court. It is the minutes taken by Captain Dmitrovic from the command of the 1st Partisan Brigade. It's a meeting that occurred on the 14th of May, 1992 with the presidents of municipalities in the zone of responsibility of the 1st -- of the division. And if you go following the agenda in the four items at the top of the page, you'll see present at the meeting, and it identifies various persons who were present at the meeting. They included the commander of the 30th Partisan Division Colonel Stanislav Galic; the commander of the 6th Partisan Brigade, Colonel Branko Basara. And you may recall, Mr. Krajisnik, that we looked at Colonel Basara's war diary last week. Colonel Basara, who later became a member of the Crisis Staff in Sanski Most. The other attendees were the Chief of Staff of the 30th -- it looks like Partisan Brigade Lieutenant-Colonel Stevan Kokovic; the commander of the territorial staff of Kljuc, I won't name him; and the presidents of six municipalities, Kljuc, Sipovo, Mrkonjic Grad, Jajce, Donji Vakuf, Bugojno. And at this meeting, Mr. Krajisnik, the various individuals [indiscernible] what their status was in their municipalities. And, Mr. Krajisnik, if you turn to page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if Your Honours turn likewise to the third page, you'll see items 1 through 6 identified. And this, Mr. Krajisnik, at this meeting two days after the strategic objectives were announced by Dr. Karadzic, the president, and I'm quoting: "The president of Mrkonjic Grad SO Milan Malidza presented the conclusions from the meeting held at Banja Luka." And further down in the next paragraph it says: "The strategic goals formulated at the meeting in Banja Luka were presented." And it identifies each of the strategic objectives. At the end of this particular meeting, according to this document, these strategic objectives were unanimously adopted. Now, Mr. Krajisnik, within two days of the enunciation of the strategic objectives, these -- it's clear from this document that these objectives were being enunciated in both a political and a military context; in other words, the word of those objectives was being disseminated. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Malidza was a deputy. He was a president of the municipality. And as he attended the meeting, he provided information about what had happened in Banja Luka. Had this been a war objective, it would have had to be transformed into an order and distributed to the units. It's evident here that this was simply a briefing at a meeting where the army was present. You have another municipality president who says in Kljuc: We want everything to be settled by peaceful means. This was a general meeting. It has nothing to do with military objectives because military objectives have to be translated into orders which are then forwarded to the units. It's evident here that these are not war objectives and they are not properly interpreted. This deputy interpreted them freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to the -- I don't think there's any disagreement between us, Mr. Krajisnik, that the strategic objectives needed to be translated into war objectives. In a few minutes we're going to come to some documents that I'm going to ask you some questions about. But I'd like to turn your attention, Mr. Krajisnik, to the next document which is found at tab 220. And this is a military document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm only going to interrupt because my learned friend made an assertion. I don't think there's any disagreement between us that the strategic objectives needed to be translated into war objectives. Could that be put, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I said to Mr. Krajisnik that I was going to be turning to those documents in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's start, Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm taking the point, Your Honour, because if an assertion like that is going to be made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact what Mr. Harmon did was to -- to summarise the answer of Mr. Krajisnik, who said that you would at least need military orders if you would give a fact to anything, and that Mr. Harmon more or less said that he did not disagree with that but that he would come to that at a later stage. But if this is a wrong understanding, Mr. Krajisnik, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was speaking about this meeting. I said had this been a war objective, there would have had to be a document in the form of an order under discussion. But however, the president of the municipality was simply briefing the others on what had happened in Banja Luka. For a command to be briefed, it would have had to come from the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say in order to implement whatever goal, you would at least -- to implement it militarily, you would need an order. And I think as a matter of fact that I think Mr. Harmon in that respect expressed that he did not disagree. Is that a correct understanding, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's a correct understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. Mr. Josse, I take it that the matter has been sufficiently clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, can you turn to the document that's found at tab 220. This is document that has been exhibited. It's Prosecution Exhibit 892, tab 58. This is a document, Mr. Krajisnik, that is from the 1st Krajina Corps command. It's dated the 21st of May, 1992. The author of this document is the assistant commander for moral guidance, Colonel Milutin Vukelic, and this is a document that was sent to all of the corps units within the 1st Krajina Corps command. I'd like to direct your attention, Mr. Krajisnik, to page 1 in the B/C/S. It's item 2, the bottom part of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would like to direct Your Honours to the top of page 2 in the English, the top paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in this document, Mr. Krajisnik, this is again a document that is only approximately a week after the strategic objectives were identified, Colonel Vukelic, in addressing all of the commands says the following, and I quote: "The constituent Serbian people who live on around 65 per cent of the area and represent more than 35 per cent of the population of BH must struggle for complete separation from the Muslim and Croat peoples and form their own state. Only after that will they be able to decide with whom and how they will unite and associate." Now, Mr. Krajisnik, that is strategic objective number 1, that Colonel Vukelic is disseminating to all of the units in the 1st Krajina Corps. That's a reference to strategic objective 1, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information, Mr. Prosecutor, and this was in the strategic objectives. But he's not referring to the strategic objectives; rather, he is referring to our general objectives. However, it is, yes, found in the first strategic objective. However, this is information for all the units; it's not an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct. We don't disagree on that, Mr. Krajisnik. And that strategic objective that Colonel Vukelic is referring to is the strategic objective that you considered to be the most important objective of the six. And you so stated that at the 16th Assembly Session, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vukelic is not invoking the strategic objective adopted on the 12th of May. He's just stating the goals of the Serbian people that predate the war by a long time; namely, that we wanted Republika Srpska which was formed in January 1992. However, a link can be established with the first strategic goal, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And my question to you that you did not answer, Mr. Krajisnik, was the first strategic objective, that is the separation of the Muslim and Croat people from the Serbian people, was the objective that you considered at the 16th Session of the Assembly to be the most important of the six strategic objectives. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was translated in this way, namely that Republika Srpska should have its own constituent unit separate from the other two ethnic communities, and that was to be our most important strategic goal in negotiations because we had already established the Serb republic and proclaimed it on the 19th of January, based on the Cutileiro Plan that we had endorsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let's go back to tab 218, the analysis on the combat readiness of the activities of the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to direct Your Honours' attention to the first paragraph at the top of 160.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krajisnik, I'd like to direct your attention to page bearing the last -- the ERN number with the last four digits of 7477.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a second to find it. I will be able to follow you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Page 139 at the lower right-hand column -- the lower right-hand of the page. Now, in -- according to this report the objectives that had been set forth, the political objectives that had been set forth, were implemented seriatim. And if we turn to this top paragraph on page 160: "Priorities in discharging set or approved tasks were selected depending on the actual stage of the war, the situation in the various areas of former Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the general social and economic circumstances, thus the prior focus for the army" --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, you said 160. I don't have 160. I have 139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your version it's page 139, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Page 139 of your version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Middle of the page, after the seven bullet points.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. 139, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to continue reading. I'll start where I left off in part: "Thus the prior focus of the Army of RS for quite some time had been to open and maintain a corridor linking the republic of Serbian Krajina through the Bosnian Krajina with Serbia. In the utilisation of the units of the Army of RS, this is still a priority, gaining control of the area of northern Bosnia and Posavina, with particular emphasis on Bosanski Brod and Derventa or gaining control over the broader area of Jajce and Paljevo has also been a priority on which our forces have focussed. In the last month and a half our operations have concentrated on the liberation of Podrinje and thereby the strategic objective of our war would be realised, one that could be defined as 'establishing contact with Serbia on the river Drina or the Drina ceasing to be a frontier.'" Now, Mr. Krajisnik, what this report is referring to in terms of implementing the tasks depending on the actual stage of the war and the situation, the first strategic objective that they referred to in this paragraph is the establishing a corridor. That's one of the express strategic objectives that was enunciated by Dr. Karadzic at the 16th Session; that's strategic objective number 2, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The corridor was a strategic objective, political strategic goal number 2, a corridor through Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And according to this same paragraph, the reference to the liberation of Podrinje, "thereby the strategic objective of our war would be realised, specifically establishing contact with Serbia on the River Drina or the Drina ceasing to be a frontier," that was also -- that was another strategic objective, isn't it? That was strategic objective number 3, wasn't it, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not the strategic objective number 3. The definition of that goal was completely different. I explained what our strategic goal was and how to -- how we were to achieve the Drina should no longer be a border, how to establish communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I'm looking at an exhibit which is P47 which are the strategic objectives, and strategic objective 3 in P47 reads in part "eliminate the Drina as a border separating Serbian states." The report on the army says that: "A strategic objective of our war would be realised, the Drina ceasing to be a frontier." That's the same objective, isn't it, Mr. Krajisnik? There's a reference to strategic objective number 3 in the army report. Do you dispute that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have also explained, if you look at the 16th Session of the Assembly, it is said there that we must fight for the Drina to no longer be a border between two worlds, whereas here it states that it shouldn't be a border between two states in 1993, mistakenly. And I have also explained how it was stated that the second congress of the SDA by Mr. Izetbegovic, namely that the Drina should not be a border psychologically with the use of passports, like we had a border between -- on the Una river with Croatia. And that should be achieved politically, like it was at Dayton. And that was our strategic goal. We did not achieve, however, the goal stated here by the army. The -- the border was not erased, it remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've been talking, Mr. Krajisnik, about what the army, how the army interpreted Dr. Karadzic's strategic objectives that he enunciated at the 16th Session. In this report, Mr. Krajisnik, it indicates that the primary focus of the RS was strategic objective number 2, establishing a corridor; and in the second -- in the latter part of the year 1992, the objective was to essentially establish contact with Serbia on the river Drina and make the Drina no longer a frontier. Now, those are two of the strategic objectives that the army, according to their own report, were implementing. And if we turn further in this report, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if Your Honours turn to pages -- page 162, I'm going to be referring to the top small paragraph and the -- some of the bullet points that follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krajisnik, if you turn to page -- the page bearing the ERN number 7479, that is page 141 of the report, the lower right-hand corner. Do you have that, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This report of the army, which was a military secret, goes on to say at the top of page 162, and I quote: "In analysing the results of the utilisation of individual units, we think that the following should be emphasised." And the first bullet point says: "The 1st Krajina Corps has preserved and expanded the existing border of Republika Srpska, broken up enemy groupings in Central Bosnia and Posavina, liberated Bosanski Brod, Jajce, and other towns, forced through and maintained a corridor through Posavina and significantly contributed to the Serbian -- the protection of the Serbian people." That, Mr. Krajisnik, is again a reflection of strategic objective number 2, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with strategic goal number 2. The army worked completely separately, guided by the situation. Please. On the 13th of May, just a day later, you can see the documents telling how Mr. Mladic, how Mrs. Plavsic, and the MUP minister interpreted them as political goals conducive to continued negotiations of the conference. I provided documents today testifying to their commitment to continuing negotiations. This is a document telling us about the conduct of the army in 1992. For the strategic goals of the 16th Session to be compulsory for the army, they would have had to be endorsed as a separate decision. The supreme commander should have had issued adequate orders to be reflected in orders of subordinate commanders to be implemented by the units. None of that was done, so there is no comparison with what the army was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, when you refer to what was said on the 13th of May, you stressed that the strategic objectives were interpreted on that day as "political goals conducive to continued negotiations of the conference." I think, as a matter of fact, that that seems not to be an answer to what Mr. Harmon is putting to you because - but Mr. Harmon will correct me if I'm wrong - does not put it to you that these strategic objectives were not pursued also through negotiations, but he puts to you that military documents describe, for example this one, the results of military operations in terms which -- and language either are identical or very much resemble what appears in the strategic objectives. So, Mr. Harmon, if I not correctly understood you, please tell me. But therefore, Mr. Krajisnik, to say: You see, we wanted to pursue these matters politically in negotiations is not an answer, I think, to what Mr. Harmon puts to you. And I think that should be clear at this moment so that we are not ending up in a kind of a -- well, in an exchange of views which finds not its basis in what in this case the other party, Mr. Harmon, says. Please proceed and keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, for your reference in tab 198, I believe, are the strategic objectives, so they may be used for reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Krajisnik, is -- for your reference as well, tab 198 should be the strategic objectives. Now, Mr. Krajisnik, let's go back to this part that I had just read to you. I'd like to take a look at the second bullet point. The second bullet point says: "The 2nd Krajina Corps has successfully defended the north-west borders of the republic at the River Una," and it then goes on and describes other actions of the army. Now, the actions of the 2nd Krajina Corps reflect, do they not, actions that are consistent with strategic objective number 4, establishing a border on the Una and the Neretva Rivers. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In 1992 they were on the Neretva and then they withdrew. However, they were positioned on the Una before the strategic goals. That border was established before any negotiations ever started. They just kept the existing border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, let's turn, Mr. Krajisnik, to the sixth bullet point. The sixth bullet point: "By taking Kamenica, Cerska, Glogova, the region of Osmaci village and Jadar, the Drina Corps has considerably expanded the free territory and will shortly have achieved the strategic task assigned to it by the Supreme Command while at the same time providing protection for the Serbian people." We know from evidence in this case that Glogova and the areas of Cerska and that area of Kamenica is in the Bratunac municipality along the Drina River. So this action I'm putting to you, Mr. Krajisnik, that was emphasised by the army deals with strategic objective number 3: "Establishing a corridor in the Drina River valley, that is eliminate the Drina as a border separating Serbian states." Do you agree or disagree with that, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, and here I'll explain, if you want me to, why I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have presented a directive issued by Mladic through one witness, Mr. Savkic, if you remember, who was describing a proposed concerted action. And that's the basis for this. The basis for this is a directive by the commander who told his units what they should actually be doing on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krajisnik, it's your evidence that the portion I've just read to you bears no relationship to strategic objective number 3?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I claim that and I also claim that in the end we didn't achieve any of the strategic goals set on the 12th of May, apart from the goal that had to do with Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I'm not discussing with you what ultimately was achieved; I'm discussing with you what the army understood to be the import of the strategic objectives and what they attempted to achieve in 1992. That's the focus of my examination on these points. Now, again, Mr. Krajisnik, I put to you: Are you asserting that these parts of the page that I have read to you saying that we think the following should be emphasised, and I read to you the first, second, and sixth bullet points, that those had nothing to do with the army attempting to achieve strategic objectives 2, 3, and 4?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exists here has nothing whatsoever to do with the strategic objectives adopted on the 12th of May, 1992, because they were neither published nor forwarded to commands for implementation in 1992. They were not known.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krajisnik, I -- I submitted to you a few minutes ago a document from the partisan brigade dated the 14th of May that contradicts what you just said. They were disseminated. We took a look at a document with -- from the 1st Partisan Brigade where the strategic objectives were disseminated to, among others, to Colonel Basara. They were disseminated to the political leaders of at least six municipalities. Do you still stand by what you just said, Mr. Krajisnik, that they were neither published nor forwarded to the commands for implementation in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You understood me perfectly well. The strategic goals are not forwarded to the army in that way, nor are they discussed. There is a procedure for that. What you referred to was a briefing held by one MP who attended that Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let's stay on the document then that I'm -- we've been looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to turn Your Honours' attention to page 163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, Mr. Krajisnik, when you said: What you referred to was a briefing held MP who attended the Assembly session, were you referring to the meeting where I think at that time Colonel Galic spoke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was a meeting in which, from what I read, it was not just briefing by a -- by an Assembly member. I mean, the role of the military in that meeting, are you saying, well, that they were just there to listen? Are you saying that they -- there was no adoption of conclusions, there was no input by the military persons that were -- attended that meeting? I mean, you described that as a meeting by which there was just some briefing by a civilian person, member of the Assembly, but then what was the role of military members being present? I mean, if it's so strictly separated as you again and again bring to our attention, this was the army, that were the civilian authorities, well, you may not have missed it that we heard a lot of evidence in which you see that the representatives of the armed forces are united with civilian authorities in some bodies and that they're discussing that -- there's coordination, there's cooperation, and you are again and again saying: Well, this is the army. If I don't see any order, then it's -- could you tell us then how you looked -- if there was such a strict operation, could you then tell us what the role of the military in such a meeting as you just discussed as being just a briefing by a member of parliament, what military had to do there, what the role was of, for example, but he was not the only one, Colonel Galic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a meeting that was probably convened by Colonel Galic, and he invited all presidents of Assemblies in order to provide support to his division. And in addition to Mr. Malidza, who was an MP, there were other presidents of municipalities as well, and there were a number of items on the agenda and a number of contributions. Mr. Malidza as an MP attending that meeting, which was broader in form, presented what he had heard in Banja Luka as an MP. And what I'm trying to say is the following: If Mr. Galic as division commander had to accept strategic goals as an obligation, then he should have received them through the line of command as an order. This, on the other hand, was just a meeting. There were a lot of such meetings on the ground, in municipalities, because municipalities supported the army. I'm not saying that they didn't know about strategic goals. I'm just pointing out the proper procedure that should have been followed in practice for a soldier, a military man, to receive a document on the basis of which he was supposed to do something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the adoption of conclusions in that meeting, from what I remember, proposed by Colonel Galic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, conclusions are various, just look at them. He must have told them that there were a lot of conclusions adopted on the 12th of May to continue the conference, to achieve a peaceful solution, et cetera, et cetera, all of them were adopted on the 12th of May. This is just a point-by-point account. The discussion was probably much broader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- what makes you -- what makes you think that the discussion was probably much broader?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Krajisnik have the document in front of him? It's tab 195.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's 195. Yes. But perhaps first since, Mr. Krajisnik, you said there were a lot of conclusions adopted on the 12th of May, but of course I was referring you to the meeting on the 14th of May, which seems to be very much that Mr. -- that Colonel Galic proposes to these mainly civilian authorities present to adopt conclusions which are all, apart from the first one, put in rather military terms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on the -- under point 3 it says that the positions achieved so far should be kept and defended without war. That's the cease-fire adopted on the 12th of May. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but still put -- and if you say: Hold the lines and preferably no further combat, that is still -- but let's not argue on one or two of them. Most of them -- I see here an army officer calling for a meeting with civilian authorities proposing to adopt conclusions which are -- well, let's then say mainly put in military terms. Whether they are exclusively in military terms is still to be seen. And in almost all of your answers you say: If I do not see an order, the army was totally separate from civilian authorities. I'm just trying to reconcile your answers with what I read here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am referring only to the strategic objectives. As for the army, I don't know whether or not they had orders as to the other things they were to do. They probably did. But what I was saying was when something had to be implemented what could he have implemented of the strategic goals in that area? Neither Sarajevo nor the corridor nor anything else. Only the cessation of hostilities. I'm only trying to assist. I don't actually know what they were saying there, but what I do know is the strategic objectives were political objectives and had nothing to do with the war. I wasn't present at this meeting. I don't know what they said, but I know that Malidza was briefing the others. And what I'm saying is: Had these been military objectives there would have been orders issues. That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then just where the language used by the military is, if not for the full hundred per cent, then at least to the gist of what they are saying, is reflecting very much the strategic objectives, that's all coincidence. Is that what you tell us? Because we went over this now for five, six, four examples, and then your answer is again and again it must be coincidence that they used the same language, or is that -- it's a wrong understanding because it has got nothing to do one with the other. And again here we have two different questions. The first question is whether these strategic objectives were meant to give instructions for the military as well; that's the first question. And the second question, clearly to be separated from the first one, is whether, right or wrong, the military understood those strategic objectives as addressed to them as well so that they would take them into consideration when planning their operations. So is it that you say they were just meant for political purposes; that's what you say? Or do you say that they were not only meant for political purposes for negotiations only, but this was also well understood by the military, because the military did not understand them as guiding them in preparing their operations? So two different questions, and I'd like to know if you -- if the second question you say: Well, no, they understood that well, then of course my next question would be is it all just coincidence that the same language, the same content more or less is used when they're talking about their operations and when you're talking about negotiations and politics? This is a bit of a long question but I hope you understood it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to your first question, there is no dispute that they were intended as political objectives. As for your second question, did the army understand them as military objectives --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is dispute about this answer because Mr. Harmon puts it to you that it was not exclusively for political purposes, but okay, let's forget about that at this moment. Your testimony is they were exclusively meant for political purposes and negotiations. So that's an answer to my first question. Now, the second question, whether this was well understood by the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the supreme commander, Mr. Karadzic, was supposed to understand that this was a military objective and issue orders to Mladic, and Mladic was to issue further orders to implement these. But as far as I know, he did not understand these objectives as military ones and the army could not have done this on their own. As for the fact that they correspond, maybe somebody did this, I don't know, but what I'm trying to explain is how things functioned. Mladic would have had to issue orders and he didn't, not that I know of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's a translation problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a translation problem. Which would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That it was Karadzic who understood --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: -- the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the transcript says. "The supreme commander, Mr. Karadzic, was supposed to understand that this was a military objective."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Next sentence, Your Honour, may be the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "... and issue orders to Mladic." And then it reads: "... and Mladic was to issue further orders to implement these."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's where we think the problem may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would that be -- Mr. Krajisnik, I'll slowly read, and please correct me where what I read does not reflect your answer. "The supreme commander, Mr. Karadzic, was supposed to understand that this was a military objective and issue orders to Mladic, and Mladic was to issue further orders to implement these, but as far as I know he did not understand these objectives as military ones and the army could not have done this on their own." Is there anything not correct, then please ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that he proposed these objectives as political objectives at the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question. My question, first of all, was whether there was anything wrong. There seems to be no translation problem. And I understood that the first orders to be given by the supreme commander and then follow-up orders further down by Mladic, that that would have been needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If that's what Mr. Krajisnik's saying, then of course I've got no problem. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we see in some of these documents that the same language is used. You say Mr. Karadzic was supposed to understand that this was a military objective and issue orders to Mladic, and Mladic was to issue further orders to implement these. But as far as you knew, he did not understand these objectives as military ones. But in the reports, including this - what was it? - the 1993 report and was it -- the report says that instructions were received from the supreme commander further and -- could someone help me out which tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is tab number 218.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 218, yes. Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour says: But as far as you knew, he did not understand these objectives as military ones. Could we know who "he" is in that regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand this to be Mladic. That's from the logic of the answer and from the sequence, I took that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'd rather assumed that, but perhaps that could just be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karadzic intended these objectives to be political ones, and it was not from -- or rather, the idea that these -- there was no idea that these should be military objectives coming from Karadzic. And Mladic's understanding was the same on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, clearly Mr. Sladojevic had somehow discerned that from the original language that the witness meant Karadzic, not Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, okay, fine. Then let's take it -- yes. In this analysis of April 1993, Mr. Krajisnik, it reads: "The strategic objectives of our war which were promptly defined and set before the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the commands and units, served as a general guideline upon which we planned the actual operations and concerted battles." And then it continues that: "The objectives were set before us rather than specific tasks spelled out, although the president of the republic as the supreme commander of the armed forces did orally assign a number of tasks which were of general and vital significance to our struggle in protecting the Serbian people and its territories." And then it says that: "The Main Staff translated the set objectives and tasks into general and individual missions." Are you saying that the objectives meant here which were not, from what I understand, operational objectives yet and still were in need of translation, is something totally different from the strategic objectives as they were adopted or proposed at the 16th Session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Completely different. This is military terminology. What they were saying is something else. The strategic objectives were not adopted as a decision on the 12th of May. Had they been, then that would have been a basis for Mr. Karadzic. The strategic objectives are a huge amount of material. They're enormous, and it was just a political groundwork. At the 16th Session it's quite clear that these were political objectives, and anyone would have understood them as such. And the fact that someone invokes them, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, and then if the creation of a corridor is described later on, it's all unrelated, it's just all coincidence? Because that's what you tell us more or less or what you say perhaps that they came to the same -- not only the same ideas but even the same language, they used the same language, but that was coincidence rather than that there was any relation between the operations and the language of the military compared to the objectives and the language used by the politicians.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, after the 12th of May, discussions were held with UNPROFOR to give or to open up a blue road in order to be able to pass through the territory. Many meetings were held in Banja Luka, and the army was present, in order to open up a corridor for humanitarian aid. In Podrinje, if you recall Mr. Salkic's testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I did put a clear question to you. When we are talking about corridors, we are not talking about a blue road. I was referring you to this analysis in which the corridor is certainly not a humanitarian corridor but is the -- well, mention is made of Posavina, northern Bosnia, so we are -- it's quite clear what kind of corridor was referred to that -- there. So I again put the same question to you, is whether the operations as described by the military and the language used by them compared to the objectives adopted by the politicians and the language in which this was done, whether that's coincidence or whether there was any link between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no link. There's no link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no link, thank you. Well, please -- well, I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Harmon. We will have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I would like to stay with the document that is found in tab 218. I'd like to refer you, Mr. Krajisnik, to pages bearing the ERN number 7479. That would be page 141. And I would like to direct your attention, Mr. Krajisnik, to the last paragraph above the first bullet point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would direct Your Honours' attention to page 163, starting at the paragraph after the first two bullet points.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, this again is under the chapeau in the report of the basic characteristics of the operational and tactical utilisation of the Army of Republika Srpska. And I quote: "I propose that corps commands continue with the execution of planned combat operations as follows." I'm going to direct your attention to a number of these points, starting with the first bullet point, Mr. Krajisnik, which deals with the 1st Krajina Corps. And it says, and I quote: "The 1st Krajina Corps to secure border towards Croatia and the Cazin Krajina and to be ready, in cooperation with the IBK and the Army of Republika Serbian Krajina, to prevent a break-through of Ustashi forces from the territory of the Cazin area and active operations by the armed forces of Croatia towards the corridor, the lifting of the blockade on Bratstvo-Jedinstvo highway," and it goes on. This execution of planned operations deals with -- again with strategic objective number 2. It deals with the protection of the corridor which was considered to be of vital strategic interest to your government. Do you agree with me, Mr. Krajisnik, that this reflects strategic objective number 2?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not that corridor. This concerns the highway to Western Slavonia. My answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take a look at the second bullet point. The second bullet point is addressed to the 2nd Krajina Corps, and it says: "The 2nd Krajina Corps to regroup its forces along the line: Petrovac-Bihac and Petrovac Krupa" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, Mr. Harmon, could Mr. Krajisnik first then tell us what corridor was mentioned here -- what corridor was meant here where he says: "To prevent a break-through of Ustashi forces from the territory of Cazin Krajina and active operations by the armed forces of Croatia towards the corridor." What corridor was meant there, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to lifting the blockade on the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo highway. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that you're referring us to something different, but I'm asking you what corridor was mentioned here, because I thought that Mr. Harmon wondered whether this was a reference to the corridor as we find them in the strategic objectives. So could you please tell us if this is not the corridor which we find in the strategic objectives, what corridor it then is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This is the corridor between the Bosnian Krajina and Semberija, yes, from Croatia, so that it would not be under threat from Croatia, that is. But I was thinking of the highway, that's why I said what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think as a matter of fact that -- let me just check for one second. Yes, Mr. Harmon specifically mentioned the corridor in his question, so would you please focus on the question put to you. But the matter has been clarified now. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The second bullet point, Mr. Krajisnik, I'll read it: "The 2nd Krajina Corps to regroup its forces along the line Petrovac-Bihac/Petrovac-Krupa shattered the Muslim forces on the stated lines, reached the right bank of the river Una and take control of the opposite bank of the river Una." Mr. Krajisnik, that is a reflection, is it not, of strategic objective number 4: Establish a border on the Una?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was a border on the Una before that. I don't know what he's talking about here, maybe another area. You know that at the 16th Session Karadzic said we got this from Cutileiro, from the international community. The international community gave us a border on the Una. And as for Petrovac, that's deeper task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. So I take your answer this has nothing to do with strategic objective number 4. That's your answer, isn't it, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with strategic objective number 4. It's quite separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's go to the fifth bullet point: "The tasks -- the planned combat operation for the Herzegovina Corps." And I will read the second sentence in that bullet point: "Thoroughly plan and prepare the offensive operation, gain control of the left bank of the river Neretva as soon as possible, and reach the administrative border of the Republic of Croatia." Again, Mr. Krajisnik, I put to you that deals with strategic objective number 4, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that in early 1992 they were at the Neretva and that they withdrew. As for the strategic objectives, they were on the Neretva and they are now trying to regain the lines they had lost. And they had been on the border with Croatia previously and then they lost that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, could I again ask you to answer to the questions. The question was not whether the positions at Neretva river have been consistent in all times. Mr. Harmon is asking you whether this -- whether this plan and preparation for an offensive operation to gain control of the left bank of the river Neretva, whether that is in any way related to the strategic objective. I mean, Mr. Krajisnik, you're doing it not for the first time that you're evading to address the matter which is clearly put to you in a question. It can well be that you've given up earlier that you want to regain terrain which would be consistent with the strategic objectives, it could well be that it has got nothing to do with it, but that is what the question is focussing at. And I'd like you to carefully listen to the question, because the previous one you said: No, this is not the corridor. And then you continue to talk about the highway, whereas asked what then that corridor was you said: Yes, yes, of course that was the corridor, but I was talking about the highway. No, you were saying: This is not the corridor. So therefore, please focus on the questions and try to answer them. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon. Yes, and Judge Hanoteau has a question, so perhaps the first -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, excuse me to interrupt Mr. Harmon. Mr. Krajisnik, please, let's maybe stop analysing all these documents. This is what I'd like to know: When there were all these movement of troops and combat, how did you get information on what happened? What did you know about what was going on in the field where you were, from where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When actions were planned, in the initial stage I knew nothing about any of them. Once they were completed, I was informed about them just as everybody was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: What do you mean like everybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean I attended a meeting and -- I would attend a meeting and they would say: Our army has liberated this or that. That was how I got my information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean you went to the meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the consultative meetings, the -- which were termed the meetings of the Presidency. We would meet and then we would be provided with information about what had happened a day or two before, where our army had liberated a certain territory. Those are the meetings I'm referring to, although there were other meetings as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said you were given information. But who is -- given by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may be wrong, but the participants in the meeting, the attendees, could have been Mr. Karadzic or a minister. It's very hard for me to say who. I did not have first-hand information, so I was not able to brief anybody at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But please refresh your memory. I mean, I'm sure that it's an important period for you. There was a war going on, there were military operations going on, large-scale operations. So how did you get that information? What was in place to get information on the military situation? You are saying that it's meetings of the Presidency, but who was reporting? Who reported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes it was Mr. Mladic, but it's hard for me to say now. Maybe a member of the Main Staff, maybe the minister of defence, maybe the minister of the MUP, maybe Mr. Karadzic. Those were the people who could have provided such information, although I'm not sure it was actually them. It might have been someone else. But the information was common knowledge; it was generally known. So I could also have learnt it from the media, from a television broadcast, for example. There was the SRNA agency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did -- were you kept informed by the civilian authorities on the ground, the municipalities, the authorities in the municipalities, or the MPs who were sitting in these municipalities? Did they keep you informed also? Excuse me, through informal discussions maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we arrived at an Assembly session, MPs informally informed others about the situation in their municipality, whether the situation was redressed. It was not a formal briefing, but I was able to find out from MPs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about yourself? Did you sometimes meet with representatives of municipalities in our office, with informal contacts, people coming to tell you what was happening on the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Presidents of municipalities, for instance from the Sarajevo region, would come. However, during sessions I would often sit down with MPs in my office and discuss various issues including those. I mean when we had sessions at Pale or Mount Jahorina. At other sessions in other places, that would have been difficult and I didn't have much contacts there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this meeting of May 14th, 1992, that's on tab 195 that we mentioned earlier, it's the meeting where military leaders are with authorities from municipalities. And among the civilians, as you said, we have the MP Malidza, you remember all that, right, because we mention all this earlier. So did you know that there were regional meetings among civilian authorities and military authorities going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was able to assume, but I didn't know specifically about that meeting in particular. I didn't know about many meetings in fact, because I didn't have contact with them. I wasn't in touch with them. On the 14th, I was on my way from Banja Luka to Belgrade by air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for example, did Mr. Malidza tell you about this meeting? It seems that it was an important meeting. So did he keep you informed as an MP, you know, that the military had convened this meeting with civilian authorities on May 14th, 1992. Were you kept informed? Not before the fact but after the fact, did anyone report? Did Mr. Malidza, for example, report to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not. Nor was that customary for an MP to give such a report. The next session was only on the 27th July for me. That's two months later on Mount Jahorina. That would have been his next opportunity to inform me, but I don't remember that he told me anything then either. I'm certain he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let me go back to the question that we were dealing with and that is the bullet point 5. I want to get a direct answer from you. The tasks of the Herzegovina Corps which were to prepare offensive operations and gain control of the left bank of the river Neretva as soon as possible, does that bear a relationship to strategic objective number 4?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No relationship at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you turn to the next bullet point, tasks assigned to the Drina Corps: "The Drina Corps, as soon as possible, shatter remaining Muslim forces in the regions of Srebrenica and Zepa and then regroup forces and orient them toward Gorazde." Now, we know that those locations are in Eastern Bosnia, Mr. Krajisnik. Do those directives to the Drina Corps have anything to do with strategic objective number 3, which was to establish a corridor in the Drina river valley and eliminate the Drina as a border separating Serb states.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with the strategic objective number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krajisnik, just before the break you gave evidence, and I'm referring to your testimony at 9:59:21. You -- your evidence was before the -- and I'm quoting. "For the strategic goals of the 16th Session to the compulsory for the army, they would have had to be endorsed as a separate decision. The supreme commander should have -- should have had issued adequate orders to be reflected in orders of subordinate commanders to be implemented by the units. None of that was done, so there is no comparison with what the army was doing." Now, in fact, Mr. Krajisnik, the army was the highest formation in the Republika Srpska that was able to achieve on the ground the strategic objectives. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in fact, the army was issued the task of implementing the strategic objectives and you knew that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's take a look at page 158 of the report on the army. Mr. Krajisnik, for your benefit it is found at page 138 in the B/C/S. It's the page with the last four ERN numbers 7476.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm referring to the top paragraph, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I will quote. It says: "In the past year, 1992, some self-organised units at the local level, the Army of Republika Srpska has grown into the highest strategic organisational formation of the Serbian people in former BH capable of realising the strategic and other objectives assigned to it by the Supreme Command and the president of Republika Srpska and its supreme commander." So again I put to you, Mr. Krajisnik, the army not only understood the strategic objectives at the 16th Session of the Assembly, but they were tasked with implementing on the ground the realisation of those objectives. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because the strategic objectives were not even adopted at the Assembly session as a separate decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, let's really focus your attention on the document that's found at tab 197. This is a document that is already in evidence. It is Exhibit P1154.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am informed that the translation for P1154, there is a new translation that is now inserted into the binder -- into the bundles that Your Honours have. And I'll be referring to this new translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- I don't remember that there was a translation issue earlier, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We looked at it, Your Honour, and there was some adjustments that needed to be made and we made those adjustments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know which ones? Because if you change translations halfway I think it would be fair if the Defence would be informed about what portions are changed so that they can verify. Then Mr. Registrar is provisionally instructed to replace Exhibit P1154, the new translation, so that would be P1154.1, taking out the old translation, but to keep the old translation for the time being so that it could be undone if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I will work with the Defence and identify those changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm confident we can agree upon this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, this document that we're looking at is the first directive issued by General Mladic. It is dated the 6th of June, 1992. It is a directive issued to the various subordinate units in the Army of the Republika Srpska by General Mladic, and I'm going to direct your attention to the paragraph 5. This is found on page 2 of the B/C/S, Mr. Krajisnik, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it's found on page 3, mid-paragraph, number 5: "Tasks of the units."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this directive for further actions issued by General Mladic reads as follows: "The 1st Krajina Corps from OG Doboj, uses its main forces to defend the attained lines, and part of its forces implements offensive actions along the main line Derventa-Modrica and Doboj-Podnovlje. The task: By persistent and active defence and in concert with the 2nd Krajina Corps maintain the attained front line. Use appropriate grouping of forces and co-action with East Bosnia Corps to break enemy forces on the lines of attack and reject him to the Sava River. Implement strong pressure on Modrica, from the west; at the same time secure the directions Slavonski Brod, Derventa, Odzak-Modrica-Tesic-Doboj from enemy actions. Upon request support air force of Serbian Republic of BH." . And then if we go over, Mr. Krajisnik, to the task assigned to the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's found, Your Honours, on page 4 of the English at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And page 3, Mr. Krajisnik, in the B/C/S. "The East Bosnia Corps defends the current lines with one part of its forces; necessary regrouping to be carried out, then use energetic actions in a joint operation with the 1st Krajina Corps to liberate Modrica, take the bridges over the Bosna River and provide secure traffic from Modrica to Bosanski Samac. Further, using strong security toward Tuzla and Zupanija, Cistiti, mop up or cleanse the territory of remaining groups and of individuals belonging to the enemy, and establish stronger connection with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; secure Zvornik-Milici-Vlasenica road: Ocistiti, mop up or cleanse Birac of remaining enemy forces." Mr. Krajisnik, this was the directive issued by General Mladic approximately less than a month after the strategic objectives were announced at the 16th Session to take the corridor. These were the directives for the corridor action, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It is not related to that, the two are totally unrelated. This whole directive is unrelated to the strategic objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, do you dispute that the corridor operation started on the 24th of June, 1992, approximately six weeks after the strategic objectives were announced in the -- at the 16th Session?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 24th of June I understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the Assembly session was on the 12th of May, if that is undisputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question to you is, Mr. Krajisnik: Do you agree with me or disagree with me that the operation to seize the corridor started on the 24th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when they started, but I know they ended on the 28th of June, which means you're probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So within about seven weeks of the announcement of the strategic objectives for General Mladic at the Assembly, one of the strategic objectives had been implemented and had been attained. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corridor was taken by military means on the 28th of June, that's correct, by military means, not political ones. I would like you to read the last sentence of this directive. It's very interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can I suggest Mr. Krajisnik just read it out, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik, if you would like to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I strictly prohibit any maltreatment of civilian, unarmed population, whereas prisoners must be treated or shall be treated pursuant to the Geneva Convention. Commander Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, now let us turn to the exhibit that is found at tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue. Mr. Krajisnik, you point to a line in this same document you consider to be important, although it was, I would say, unrelated to the question put to you by Mr. Harmon from what I see. Did you draw our attention to it because you considered it important for us to see that these instructions were given or is it because you consider this to be an instruction which was implemented on the ground? Is it -- we heard quite some evidence on -- on the treatment of civilian population, and we heard also some information about prisoners. And I take it that the text just say "prisoners" and not "prisoners of war." But is it because you take the position that this instruction was implemented, in general terms of course? I would not -- is that your position or is it -- or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. I don't know how it was implemented. I just thought it was interesting to bear in mind that somebody sent out something like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say, at least that is how it is translated: "I don't know how it was implemented," which suggests that it was implemented. Do you say: I don't know how it was implemented, or do you say: I don't know whether it was implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how it was implemented. I don't even know whether it was implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That provides me with the -- with an answer. Please, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to refer Your Honours to two exhibits. One I'm going to distribute, and the other, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krajisnik, that is found in tab 217. These are related documents.
